title: Chess basics
examples: How does the queen move across the board?
What is the difference between check and checkmate?
Can I capture a piece that is blocking the way?

explain.say: Today we learn how the chess pieces move around the board.
The rook moves like a plus sign on the board.
The knight moves in a special 'L' shape pattern.
When a piece attacks the king, we say it is in check.

items: You must get the king out of danger

explain.say: If the king is in check and cannot escape, it is checkmate.

items: No piece can block the attack
No piece can capture the attacker

explain.say: If you are playing in real life, remember to always check the rules.

faq.q: What is the difference between check and checkmate?
faq.a: Check means the king is currently under attack by an opponent's piece. Checkmate means the king is under attack and there is no legal move to escape that attack.
asks: When is the king in danger?
What does it mean if the king cannot move?

faq.q: Can I capture a piece that is blocking the way?
faq.a: Yes, if the piece you are moving can legally jump over or land on the square occupied by the opponent's piece, you can capture it.
asks: Does blocking always stop a move?

faq.q: Does the knight move like a straight line?
faq.a: No, the knight moves in a specific 'L' shape pattern, which is two squares in one direction and then one square perpendicular to that direction.
asks: What is the knight's unique move?
Does the knight follow straight lines?

faq.q: What happens when I make a move that leaves my king in check?
faq.a: If your move leaves your own king in check, it is an illegal move, and you must correct it.
asks: Is it okay to put my king in danger?
What is an illegal move in chess?

faq.q: Can the queen move like any other piece?
faq.a: The queen is very powerful because it combines the moves of the rook and the bishop, meaning it moves straight or diagonally any number of squares.
asks: Is the queen the strongest piece?
What moves can the queen make?

facts: The king must never be left in check.
The knight is the only piece that can jump over other pieces.
The queen combines the moves of the rook and the bishop.

quiz.say: A piece moves straight across or diagonally any number of squares. Which piece is this?
quiz.why: The queen combines the straight and diagonal movements of the rook and bishop.

wrong.0: The bishop cannot move straight across the board.
wrong.1: The knight must always move in an 'L' shape.
wrong.3: The rook cannot move diagonally at all.

quiz.say: If a king is attacked and cannot escape, what has happened?
quiz.why: Checkmate means the king is attacked and all escape routes are blocked.

wrong.0: Stalemate means the king is safe but has no legal moves.
wrong.1: Capturing a piece does not automatically end the game.
wrong.3: Check only means the king is currently attacked, not that the game is over.

quiz.say: A piece moves two squares and then one square sideways in an 'L' shape. Which piece is this?
quiz.why: The knight's unique movement pattern is the 'L' shape, which allows it to jump over pieces.

wrong.0: Pawns only move forward one square at a time.
wrong.1: The rook only moves in perfectly straight lines.
wrong.2: The king moves only one square in any direction.
